boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: A corridor-by-corridor set of named destinations in the walkable campus-to-downtown area, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Bagels across El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: El Camino Real corridor, opposite SCU’s main entrance
cards.notes: Cross to 495 El Camino Real for the bakery’s own bagel, breakfast-bagel, sandwich, smoothie, and lunch menu; check its site before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A directly opposite-campus stop with a broad bagel and sandwich menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Cramer's Bagels lists its Santa Clara address as 495 El Camino Real and offers bagels, breakfast bagels, bagel sandwiches, smoothies, and more.
cards.access_notes: Business hours and menu availability are published by the business; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Mission history on El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: El Camino Real corridor at SCU’s western edge
cards.notes: Use the Mission’s official history page to orient yourself before viewing the church from the El Camino Real side of the campus corridor.
cards.short_summary: The university’s documented historic Mission anchors the El Camino Real edge.
cards.evidence_claim: SCU identifies Mission Santa Clara de Asís as the eighth mission site in California and says the current church was built in 1927–28.
cards.access_notes: This destination is at the campus edge; respect church services and any posted access guidance.

cards.title: Portuguese pastry on El Camino Real
cards.subtitle: El Camino Real corridor, east of SCU
cards.notes: Head to 1085 El Camino Real if you want a pastry-stop option; the city’s visitor bureau specifically identifies the shop and its pastel de nata.
cards.short_summary: A named El Camino Real bakery documented for Portuguese pastries.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Santa Clara lists Portuguese Tasty Desserts at 1085 El Camino Real and describes its pastel de nata as a Portuguese custard tart.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara Global Games Food Trail
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; verify current business hours directly before going.

cards.title: Thai menu in Franklin Mall
cards.subtitle: Franklin Mall corridor, near Mission Branch Library
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s online menu to plan a carryout or dine-in meal at 1211 Franklin Mall; vegetarian options are listed among its food types.
cards.short_summary: A Franklin Mall restaurant with an official menu and vegetarian options.
cards.evidence_claim: Jasmine Thai Cuisine lists its location as 1211 Franklin Mall and identifies Thai dishes and vegetarian options on its official ordering site.
cards.access_notes: The business posts separate dining, carryout, and delivery hours; check before visiting.

cards.title: Fountain at Franklin Square
cards.subtitle: Franklin Mall corridor at Monroe Street and Franklin Street
cards.notes: Pause at the Old Town Quad fountain while moving through Franklin Square; the city describes it as a waiting place for nearby bus passengers.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed fountain in the Old Town Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara places Franklin Square Fountain at Monroe Street and Franklin Street and describes it as surrounded by small fountains in the Old Town Quad.
cards.source_title: Franklin Square Fountain — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork; follow any on-site rules and street-event closures.

cards.title: Public art at 1200 Franklin Mall
cards.subtitle: Franklin Mall corridor, Franklin Square area
cards.notes: Add this named city-listed artwork to a Franklin Mall walk, and consult the city’s public-art map for its recorded address and nearby works.
cards.short_summary: A distinct public-art stop in the Franklin Mall corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara’s Art & Statues map lists the artwork Indians and Pioneers at 1200 Franklin Mall, Santa Clara.
cards.source_title: Art & Statues — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork; view from public areas and observe any posted rules.

cards.title: Market at Jackson and Homestead
cards.subtitle: Jackson Street–Homestead Road corridor, downtown edge
cards.notes: Plan a Saturday morning loop around the market corner at Jackson Street and Homestead Road; confirm the specific date in the city calendar first.
cards.short_summary: A city-calendar market stop at a named downtown corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara calendar locates the Santa Clara Farmers Market at the corner of Jackson Street and Homestead Road and lists a 9 a.m.–1 p.m. event time.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara Farmers Market — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: The cited calendar occurrence is dated; check the current city calendar for market dates and vendor participation.

cards.title: Ice-cream tacos on Park Avenue
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue corridor beside The Alameda near SCU
cards.notes: Walk the Park Avenue block near The Alameda for a dessert stop; the official visitor guide identifies the shop’s waffle-cone taco shells and address.
cards.short_summary: A named Park Avenue dessert shop documented by the city visitor bureau.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Santa Clara lists Rocko’s Ice Cream Tacos at 2905 Park Avenue and describes waffle-cone taco shells filled with ice cream.
cards.source_title: Santa Clara Global Games Food Trail
cards.access_notes: Food requires purchase; consult the business directly for current operating hours.

cards.entity_name: Voyager Craft Coffee — Alameda Santa Clara
cards.title: Coffee on The Alameda
cards.subtitle: The Alameda corridor, northwest of campus
cards.notes: Use Voyager’s location page to find its Alameda Santa Clara shop at 2221 The Alameda, then verify operating status and hours before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A named coffee location on The Alameda with published daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Voyager Craft Coffee lists its Alameda Santa Clara location at 2221 The Alameda and publishes daily 7 a.m.–5 p.m. hours.
cards.access_notes: The business’s location page lists daily hours; verify current operating status before going.

cards.title: Downtown blocks at Franklin Square
cards.subtitle: Franklin Street–Benton Street–Monroe Street–Jackson Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Franklin Square as the connective stop for a downtown walk; the city identifies its surrounding streets and describes its city-owned parking areas.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown complex bounded by four documented streets.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Santa Clara identifies Franklin Square parking lots as adjacent to Benton, Monroe, Jackson, and Homestead Road, and says the complex is maintained by the Downtown Parking Maintenance District.
cards.source_title: Franklin Square Paid Parking Project — City of Santa Clara
cards.access_notes: This is a public downtown complex; parking policies and event conditions may change.
